title: Caerlum Rising Revisited
premise: Tamsin Thornbury, a mercenary whose god Caerlum fell silent five years ago, survives by selling harmless charms in Greyhallow, a city where magic is outlawed and the godless are watched. When a dying courier presses a map into Tamsin's hands, they discover it marks the resting place of Caerlum's stolen heart—the source of the god's silence and the seed of a war the old kingdoms buried. Hunted by the Inquisition and shadowed by Veyra, a former comrade who wants the heart for herself, Tamsin must choose between restoring a god who abandoned them and destroying the last piece of divinity to keep the world free. In the end, Tamsin shatters the heart, losing their memories of Caerlum entirely, and walks out of Greyhallow as no one's servant—and, for the first time, entirely their own.
about_author: Astrid Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal cottage, accompanied by a deaf terrier and an unreasonable number of half-finished maps.

chapters.title: The Godless Quarter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the market of Greyhallow, Tamsin sells charms that no longer work, hiding their past as a sworn blade of the silent god Caerlum. A routine day establishes the city's fear of magic and Tamsin's careful invisibility. The emotional beat is weary resignation—the ache of serving a god who no longer answers.

chapters.title: Blood on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A stranger staggers into Tamsin's shop at closing, bleeding from an Inquisitor's blade, and presses a rolled map into Tamsin's hands before dying with Caerlum's name on his lips. Tamsin hides the body and the map, terrified. The beat is dread: invisibility is over.

chapters.title: What the Map Promises
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Deciphering the map by candlelight, Tamsin recognizes the sigils of Caerlum's old order and a location: the Hollow Vault, where something of the god lies hidden. Flashbacks reveal the day the god went silent. The beat is reluctant hope curdling into suspicion—why them?

chapters.title: The Inquisition Knocks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inquisitor Hale arrives with questions about the dead courier. Tamsin lies badly, and Hale leaves a warning rather than an arrest—she suspects more than she can prove. The beat is claustrophobic pressure; the noose tightens.

chapters.title: A Face from the War
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra, once Tamsin's shield-sister, arrives in Greyhallow tracking the map for her own patrons. She watches Tamsin from the crowd, torn between old loyalty and ambition. The beat is bittersweet nostalgia sharpening into calculation.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin seeks out Doss, a smuggler, to buy passage out of the city, paying with a forbidden relic. Doss warns that the roads are watched and someone else is asking about the Vault. The beat is uneasy alliance; escape has a price.

chapters.title: Veyra at the Door
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Veyra confronts Tamsin at night, offering partnership: together they can reach the Vault before the Inquisition. Tamsin refuses, remembering Veyra's betrayal at the war's end. The beat is old wounds reopened, trust refused.

chapters.title: Flight from Greyhallow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inquisition raiders hit the shop; Tamsin flees through the sewers with the map and joins Doss's caravan. Hale finds the ransacked shop and realizes the charm seller was Caerlum's sworn blade. The beat is adrenaline and loss—everything left behind burns.

chapters.title: The Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the road through a battlefield left from the old war, Tamsin encounters ghosts of the god's silence—shrines defaced, prayers unanswered. A fever dream shows Caerlum's heart being torn out. The beat is grief for a god and a self that no longer exist.

chapters.title: Veyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra negotiates with her patrons—the Ashen Conclave, who want the heart to crown a new god they can control. She justifies her ambition but hesitates when she learns what the ritual demands. The beat is ambition at war with buried conscience.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Doss's caravan is ambushed by Conclave agents; Doss dies buying Tamsin time. Tamsin kills for the first time in five years and feels Caerlum stir faintly at the violence—proof the god isn't gone, only caged. The beat is horror and terrible hope.

chapters.title: Hale's Pursuit
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale follows the trail of bodies, increasingly convinced the Inquisition's masters want the heart for themselves. She interrogates a captured Conclave agent and learns the truth of the coming war. The beat is disillusionment—duty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Shrine in the Marsh
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sheltering at a hidden shrine, Tamsin prays for the first time in years and receives a fragmented vision: the Vault, the heart, and a choice—restore the god or unmake it. The beat is communion after long silence, and the terror of being chosen again.

chapters.title: Shield-Sisters Divided
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra intercepts Tamsin at the marsh's edge; instead of fighting, they share a night of memories and truths. Veyra admits the Conclave's plan; Tamsin admits they want the god back. Neither trusts the other, but they travel together. The beat is fragile reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Gates of the Hollow Vault
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The pair reach the Vault, sealed with blood-sigils only a sworn blade can open. Tamsin's blood unlocks the gates, triggering alarms that echo across the valley—Hale and the Conclave both converge. The beat is point of no return.

chapters.title: What the God Remembered
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Inside, murals reveal the truth: Caerlum's followers tore out their own god's heart to stop a war, and the silence was mercy, not abandonment. Tamsin's faith inverts. The beat is devastating clarity—everything Tamsin mourned was a lie they needed.

chapters.title: The Conclave Arrives
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The Conclave seizes the Vault; Veyra is ordered to bind Tamsin for the ritual. Instead she turns on her patrons, buying Tamsin seconds with her blades. Hale arrives amid the chaos, forced to choose sides. The beat is betrayal repaid with sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Heart of Caerlum
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Before the caged heart, Tamsin hears Caerlum's true voice—offering restoration, power, vengeance. The god's whisper is seductive and corrupting. Hale holds the Conclave off at the doors. The beat is the darkest temptation: everything Tamsin ever was, offered back.

chapters.title: The Shattering
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Understanding that a restored god means an endless war reborn, Tamsin drives their old sworn-blade through the heart. The explosion of divine light erases every memory Tamsin holds of Caerlum—the god, the war, the vows. The beat is terrible, liberating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ash and Silence
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale surveys the ruined Vault, the Conclave broken, Veyra dying but at peace. She finds Tamsin alive but hollow-eyed, remembering nothing of the god or their sworn past—and chooses to let them go, falsifying her report. The beat is mercy from an unlikely hand.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller, Again
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Back in Greyhallow, Tamsin reopens the shop with no memory of why their hands know old sigils, why Veyra's name brings grief, or why the silent shrines feel like mourning. A customer asks if the charms work. Tamsin smiles: 'They keep what matters.' The beat is quiet rebirth.

chapters.title: What Remains Unwritten
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shifting POVs. Veyra's letter, unsent, sits in Hale's desk; the Conclave's remnants scatter; and in a marsh shrine, something small and new flickers where Caerlum died—neither god nor gone. Tamsin, unnamed and unsworn, closes shop at dusk. The beat is open-ended peace: identity remade, memory a price worth paying.
